title: GS1 RF Processing

children:
When checking into your warehouse product that uses GS1 barcodes, the 
 RF receipt processing flow is somewhat different than it is when scanning 
 typical barcodes. GS1 barcodes contain multiple informational segments 
 (called application identifiers), such as quantity, lot, or license plate 
 ID. As a result, the system presents the RF user with a different set 
 of screens to scan in the GS1 barcode data. The goal of this topic is to illustrate the differences in the RF receiving 
 flow when scanning GS1 barcodes. You can view steps for the typical RF 
 check in flow by visiting one of the topics in the "Related Procedures" 
 section below.
The following GS1 RF receipt check in scenarios are discussed in this topic:

Entering Missing Information During 
 Receipt Check In

Receipt Check In With Lots / Expiration 
 Dates

Receipt Check In With Serial Number 
 Tracking
Receipt Check In With Catch Weights

Check In & Locate (Immediate) and 
 Quick Receive Execution Methods
The following buttons actions are used in GS1 RF screens:

Accepts previously scanned data, and the system proceeds to the next 
 GS1 scan screen.

Returns the user to the receiving preferences screen without processing 
 the check in.

This button appears after one complete set of scans has been performed 
 for a label, and the system displays the first scan screen for the next 
 item to be checked in. When you press this button, the system will execute 
 all the post-check-in processing (locating, etc.), and return you to the 
 initiation screen.

The system allows you to skip a scan (for example, maybe the barcode 
 is smudged and would not be readable by the RF device). When you skip 
 a scan, the system will prompt you to manually enter the information that 
 the system would have acquired via the scan.

System disregards previously scanned information, and will navigate 
 back to the GS1 scan screen. Also, the system will reset the scan number 
 back to 1.

When initiating a basic RF Check In action, the system requires one 
 or more of the following values: item,        item cross reference,        quantity,        quantity unit of measure, and        container ID.  The 
 user enters this information using the Enter Item, Check In and Container 
 ID screens.  For 
 GS1 processing, the system replaces these screens with a single GS1 Scan 
 screen. As in typical RF processing, the user may rescan, skip, or cancel 
 when scanning GS1 barcodes. Note that the quantity UM is not directly 
 defined on the GS1 barcode; instead, this is associated with an item cross 
 reference record (in absence of this, the system uses the item's base 
 unit of measure). If configured to do so, the system can also display 
 a verification screen after each scan.

Note that example application identifiers 
 are in parenthesis below each screen diagram. These could be mapped to 
 different values depending on your configurations.

Manual 
 Container Assignment (two items, 
 two GS1 barcodes each to scan)

Manual 
 Container Assignment (two items, 
 two GS1 barcodes each to scan, scan verification on)

System 
 Container Assignment (two items, 
 two GS1 barcodes total to scan)

Entering Missing Information During 
 Receipt Check In

In cases where the GS1 barcode does not provide enough information for 
 SCALE to check in an item (such as if the barcode is smudged or ripped), 
 the system will display a screen that prompts the user to enter in this 
 additional data. The example below assumes that the user attempted to scan the first barcode, but it was smudged, and no value was readable. The system would then take the user back to the first scan screen so all working scans (scan 2) would be redone, and the information from the bad barcode (scan 1) would be manually entered:

Quantity 
 Not Provided By GS1 Barcode (manual 
 container assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)
item A, first scan w/smudged barcode
(item cross ref). User presses Skip Button.

user now prompted to enter "missing" data 
 from the first scan

Receipt Check In With Lots / Expiration 
 Dates

If you are receiving items into your warehouse that use lot/expiration 
 date tracking, these may be represented by a separate GS1 barcode. As 
 seen in the example below, this adds another scan screen to the RF flow:

Items 
 Lot / Expiration Date Tracked (manual 
 container assignment, two items, three GS1 barcodes each to scan)

Receipt Check In With Serial Number 
 Tracking

If you are receiving items into your warehouse that use serial number 
 tracking, these may be represented on the barcode that includes the item 
 or item cross reference number. Note that a quantity value is not needed, 
 as the system assumes that the quantity is 1 EA, because a serial number 
 would only be assigned to one single unique item:

Items 
 Serial Number Tracked (manual 
 container assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)
GS1 Processing and Serial Number Ranges

During the processing of GS1 scans, since the system allows the scanning of only a single serial number from a GS1 barcode, the system ignores a serial number template's "allow range entry" setting. You will, however, be able to enter serial number ranges as part of the normal check in process that occurs after the GS1 scan(s).
Receipt Check In With Catch Weights

If you are receiving items into your warehouse that use catch weight 
 tracking, this value can be represented by a GS1 barcode, but this is not currently supported by SCALE. Instead, you 
 will need to enter this value manually after the scans for an item have 
 been completed:

Items 
 Catch Weight Tracked (manual 
 container assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)
user manually enters catch weight value for item

You will encounter this flow if, for example, your warehouse prefers 
 to nest containers onto pallets during check in, for example. In order 
 to activate this nesting, you need to have the "Nest During Check 
 In" option selected on your receiving preferences. After you scan 
 the GS1 barcodes of the containers you are going to nest, the system will 
 display an additional screen for the parent container (such as a pallet) 
 you want to nest into. Note that this functionality is not available in 
 the separate RF main menu function "Receipt Container Nesting."

Nesting 
 Containers During Check In (manual 
 container assignment, two items [containers], two GS1 barcodes each to 
 scan, one parent container)
user scans ID of parent container

Check In & Locate (Immediate) 
 and Quick Receive Execution Methods

These two execution methods vary the GS1 RF flow slightly, as seen in 
 the following examples:

Check 
 In & Locate Execution Method (manual 
 container assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)
system locates product immediately; item B scan starts...

With the Quick Receiving (User) execution method, the system checks in and 
 locates the container(s) that you enter, and provides separate screens 
 for each entity checked in that allows the user to indicate where they 
 want the container to be putaway. The system does not create putaway work 
 using this method. There is also a Quick Receiving (System) method, where the system provides the location value and the user cannot change it.

Quick 
 Receiving (User) Execution Method (manual 
 container assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)

system navigates back to initiation screen, so user can 
 check in another receipt

With the item initiation method, the system asks for an item, and then 
 the user chooses the receipt they want to receive against. For GS1 processing, 
 you select the receipt you are checking in after the GS1 scans:

Item 
 Initiation Method (manual container 
 assignment, two items, two GS1 barcodes each to scan)
user indicates the receipt they are checking in

GS1 RF Processing

        
When checking into your warehouse product that uses GS1 barcodes, the 
 RF receipt processing flow is somewhat different than it is when scanning 
 typical barcodes. GS1 barcodes contain multiple informational segments 
 (called application identifiers), such as quantity, lot, or license plate 
 ID. As a result, the system presents the RF user with a different set 
 of screens to scan in the GS1 barcode data. The goal of this topic is to illustrate the differences in the RF receiving 
 flow when scanning GS1 barcodes. You can view steps for the typical RF 
 check in flow by visiting one of the topics in the "Related Procedures" 
 section below.

        
 

        
 

        
Related Topics...

        
GS1 Setup Overview
        

        
GS1 Process Summary
        

        
Checking In and Locating Product 
 (RF)
        

        
 

        
 

        
The following GS1 RF receipt check in scenarios are discussed in this topic:

        
- General Button Actions

- Receipt Check In With Lots / Expiration

- Receipt Check In With Serial Number 
 Tracking

        
- Receipt Check In With Catch Weights

        
- Nesting Containers During Check In

        
- Check In & Locate (Immediate) and 
 Quick Receive Execution Methods

        
- Item Initiation Method

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
General Button Actions





        
The following buttons actions are used in GS1 RF screens:

        
 

        

            
            
            

                

                    
Button

OK

                

                

                    
Accepts previously scanned data, and the system proceeds to the next 
 GS1 scan screen.

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
Cancel
                    

                    
 

                

                

                    
Returns the user to the receiving preferences screen without processing 
 the check in.

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
Done
                    

                

                

                    
This button appears after one complete set of scans has been performed 
 for a label, and the system displays the first scan screen for the next 
 item to be checked in. When you press this button, the system will execute 
 all the post-check-in processing (locating, etc.), and return you to the 
 initiation screen.

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
Skip
                    

                    
 

                

                

                    
The system allows you to skip a scan (for example, maybe the barcode 
 is smudged and would not be readable by the RF device). When you skip 
 a scan, the system will prompt you to manually enter the information that 
 the system would have acquired via the scan.

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
Rescan
                    

                

                

                    
System disregards previously scanned information, and will navigate 
 back to the GS1 scan screen. Also, the system will reset the scan number 
 back to 1.

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
 Basic GS1 Receipt Check In...



        
When initiating a basic RF Check In action, the system requires one 
 or more of the following values: item,        item cross reference,        quantity,        quantity unit of measure, and        container ID.  The 
 user enters this information using the Enter Item, Check In and Container 
 ID screens.  For 
 GS1 processing, the system replaces these screens with a single GS1 Scan 
 screen. As in typical RF processing, the user may rescan, skip, or cancel 
 when scanning GS1 barcodes. Note that the quantity UM is not directly 
 defined on the GS1 barcode; instead, this is associated with an item cross 
 reference record (in absence of this, the system uses the item's base 
 unit of measure). If configured to do so, the system can also display 
 a verification screen after each scan.

        
 

        
Note that example application identifiers 
 are in parenthesis below each screen diagram. These could be mapped to 
 different values depending on your configurations.

rows.text:
Accepts previously scanned data, and the system proceeds to the next 
 GS1 scan screen.

Returns the user to the receiving preferences screen without processing 
 the check in.

This button appears after one complete set of scans has been performed 
 for a label, and the system displays the first scan screen for the next 
 item to be checked in. When you press this button, the system will execute 
 all the post-check-in processing (locating, etc.), and return you to the 
 initiation screen.

The system allows you to skip a scan (for example, maybe the barcode 
 is smudged and would not be readable by the RF device). When you skip 
 a scan, the system will prompt you to manually enter the information that 
 the system would have acquired via the scan.

System disregards previously scanned information, and will navigate 
 back to the GS1 scan screen. Also, the system will reset the scan number 
 back to 1.
